title: The drop's look: the demo's capsule burn and thermal shell, the mechs' fire and smoke streaming up instead of an orange bubble, rubble at each touchdown, the demo's ant view with a lowered near plane, and a screenshot chord that no longer skips the cut
context: Owner, 2026-10-23 09:30 JST, after the first test of the FEIDS-26 drop on localhost:8155: 'I could not take screenshots because any key press cancels the animation; FEIDS animation changes; the blue flames and burn animation needs work 2) the mechs too are surrounded by an orange bubble, it should be a more believable mix of re-entry burn and smoke/wind effects. 3) more rubbles when they land. 4) I insist on having the same ant-view extreme low angle with one leg of the last Mech in the foreground, as in the demo.' Spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-drop-fx-design.md (decisions, implemented as written); the demo's sources in the vault (stalheart-feids26-peek: ridgeback-drop_effects.js, feids26_viewer.js, feids26_shield-heat.js). Branch drop-fx from overnight-2026-10-23, not pushed.
outcome: Screenshots: src/fx/camera-shot.js skipsOn(ev): a keydown with Cmd, Ctrl or Alt held, or a modifier key alone, lets every skippable shot run; other keys and taps still skip. The ant view: REINFORCEMENTS.timeline.ground is the demo's (9.75, 0.2, 7) m, fov 48 -> 67 over [16.5, 18] s, the demo's shake behind the knob shot.shake (1 = demo); while the cut runs the host sets the camera's near to shot.near 0.00025 units (~0.19 m) and the rule's fov each tick, putting back the values it found at the shot's end, on restore, and (near only) under a seat; no z-fighting seen, near not raised. The drop also waits for the hull's deploy (the host's shotActive is a shot or the deploy), which outranked the cut's camera and hid its first seconds. New src/fx/feids-heat.js ports the demo's effects as functions of the drop's clock, pooled once at begin(): each capsule's heat group (blue glow, white rim, 24 flame trails over the spindle PROFILE, pulsing as the demo) at the shell's axis and the thermal emissive on clones of the GLB's materials (heat before the split, exp(-1.8 split) after); each falling mech's 45 fire sprites rising behind it plus 16 grey wind-pulled smoke sprites above (the orange sphere removed); at each touchdown the demo's 42 smoke sprites, its crack lines and 24 rock chunks (one InstancedMesh a mech, thrown 6..11 m/s out and 4..8 up, resting and staying until release()); the game's dust twice for the laggard.
alternatives: Keeping the 3.5 m ground camera of 2026-10-23 because of the 3 m near plane: the owner insisted on the demo's angle, so the near plane moves for the cut instead.
Particles with history (a pool advanced each frame): the demo's functions of time survive a skip, a slow frame or a seek with the same picture, and need no per-frame state.
Steering the chunks away from the ant camera: not done; two of the laggard's land beside the lens and read as boulders in front of the trio's feet at 22 s (left for the owner's eye).
evidence: npm test 303 programs (new: camera-shot-skip, feids-heat), npm run check (td-tab 5,322 under 5,450), npm run architecture, npm run build: green on the final tree.

--reinforcements (port 18184): Cmd, Cmd+Shift+4 and Shift at drop t 1.22 s leave the cut on (lens near 0.00025, fov 48); a plain K at 27.37 s ends it, lens put back; touchdowns heard at 13.02 / 13.43 / 14.02 / 19.23 s; the four plus the drop's effects cost 640 draw calls at drop t 25.6 s (608 before the effects); PASS through reinforce-arena.
--reinforcements-lull PASS: called day 1, due day 4, dropping on day 4 at a lull, four landed.

--feids-shots PASS: frames at drop t 3.03, 7.1, 13.05, 17.1, 19.7, 22.08 s (artifacts/browser/feids-<t>.png), the cut live and near 0.00025 through 19.7 s, fov 67 from 19.6 s, four mechs and the lens put back at the end. Seen: 3 s the capsules shield-first, white rim, red thermal band, blue trails streaming up; 7 s the quarters cooling, the first pair's flames and smoke streaming up behind them; 13 s the first mech's chunks leaving its feet over the cracks; 17 s the camera turning up toward the laggard (sky only); 19.6 s the laggard's foot filling the right of the frame in its dust; 22 s the laggard towering, its leg in the foreground, the trio on the horizon, the rubble round the lens.
